The cost is worse MAE (more far-off errors) and weaker mild-class F1. One fold only, wide CI — go/no-go signal, not a benchmark. Justified the full 5-fold validation. ALL fold-1 numbers recomputed and confirmed exactly.

configs.full_name: STEP 1 — full 5-fold validation of greedy per-item CoT (pooled OOF n=1752)
configs.summary: Repeat the greedy CoT probe across all 5 folds and pool OOF (n=1752) to get a real paired mean+/-std vs MentalBERT+CORN, killing fold-1 luck.

steps.title: Array over 5 folds
steps.detail: run_cot_probe_folds.sbatch array 1-5; each fold scored on its own held-out OOF slice with the same greedy CoT and Hybrid-W3 evidence.

steps.title: Pool OOF predictions
steps.detail: build_cot_report.py auto-pools outputs/cot/folds/*.csv into pooled OOF n=1752.

steps.title: Paired mean+/-std + t-test
steps.detail: Report per-fold mean+/-std and a paired-t card for macro-F1, QWK, MAE vs the matched encoder rows (std uses ddof=1).

steps.title: Recompute per-class F1 pooled
steps.detail: Pooled per-class F1 to confirm/deny the severe-class recovery and check whether encoder class-3 F1 is truly zero (it was a fold-1 artifact).

configs.methodology: Same as probe but across all 5 participant-grouped folds, greedy, Hybrid-W3 evidence, per-item independent scoring. Pooled OOF n=1752. Paired comparison to MentalBERT+CORN with per-fold paired t-test (crit t<2.78 for 4 dof). NOTE: the file cot_feasibility_metrics.json is actually this pooled 5-fold artifact (n=1752), not a fold-1-only file.

results.note: Delta +0.030, CoT wins 4/5 folds, t=+2.30 (CONFIRMED, std=ddof1; held up, not formally sig at .05)
Delta -0.039, encoder wins 4/5, t=-1.24 (CONFIRMED); REVERSED from fold-1 (fold-1 QWK win was luck)
Delta +0.070 worse, encoder wins 4/5, t=+3.42 (CONFIRMED, robust)
pooled; enc class-3 F1 is 0.159 NOT zero (0.000 was fold-1-specific) (CONFIRMED)

configs.verdict: Untrained few-shot CoT robustly beats the trained encoder on macro-F1 + accuracy + severe-class recovery, but the encoder is robustly better on ORDINAL metrics (QWK, MAE) because CoT errs farther when wrong. The fold-1 QWK win was fold luck. Net: complementary, not dominant — motivates self-consistency (cut far-off errors) and an ensemble (58% disagreement). All pooled per-fold numbers + t-stats recomputed and confirmed.

configs.full_name: STEP 2 — self-consistency CoT (N=5 chains, T=0.7, majority vote)
configs.summary: Sample 5 CoT chains at T=0.7 and majority-vote to cut far-off errors — it trims MAE/far-off but erodes the severe-class macro-F1 edge, so it is NOT the lever.

steps.title: Sample N=5 chains
steps.detail: Probe optimized to batch N chains via num_return_sequences at T=0.7; sc5 fold ~22 min (~2x greedy, not 5x).

steps.title: Majority vote
steps.detail: Vote across the 5 chains per item; also emit vote-fraction prob_0..3 as calibrated soft probabilities for later probability-averaging.

steps.title: Pool OOF and compare to greedy
steps.detail: Compare sc5 vs greedy CoT on macro-F1, severe-class F1, MAE, far-off, QWK at pooled n=1752.

steps.title: Compare to encoder
steps.detail: Paired comparison vs encoder on QWK/MAE/macro-F1 with per-fold win counts and t-stats.

configs.methodology: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, no training, Hybrid-W3 evidence; N=5 sampled chains at temperature 0.7 via num_return_sequences; per-item majority vote for the label and vote fractions for prob_0..3. Pooled OOF n=1752.

results.note: voting regresses toward modal/safe label, erodes bold severe calls (CONFIRMED)
still wins but weaker than greedy's +0.030 (CONFIRMED)

configs.verdict: Self-consistency is NOT the lever: voting regresses toward the modal/safe label, eroding exactly the bold severe-class calls that gave CoT its macro-F1 edge. The QWK/MAE gap is structural, not variance. Greedy CoT remains the better standalone CoT config. The durable payoff of sc5 is the calibrated prob_0..3 it provides for probability-averaging in the ensemble (STEP 3). All numbers confirmed from cot_feasibility_metrics_sc5.json.

configs.full_name: STEP 3 — CoT + encoder ensembles (prob-avg 50/50, severity-routed, nested-CV blend)
configs.summary: Combine the complementary CoT and encoder predictions; severity-routed (trust CoT when it calls >=2) beats BOTH parents on macro-F1 and QWK simultaneously.

steps.title: Load paired OOF
steps.detail: src/evaluation/cot_ensemble.py reuses existing paired OOF (encoder CORN probs + CoT greedy labels + sc5 vote-fraction probs); NO GPU.

steps.title: Probability-average 50/50
steps.detail: Average encoder CORN probs with sc5 CoT vote fractions 50/50 (soft probs required; a hard one-hot CoT degenerates to the CoT prediction).

steps.title: Severity-gated routing
steps.detail: Use greedy-CoT label when its prediction is >=2 (severe), else use the encoder; rule chosen from the prior severe-class finding, not label-tuned.

steps.title: Nested-CV linear blend
steps.detail: Leakage-free per-fold blend weight on CoT: {1:.4,2:.8,3:.8,4:.6,5:.6}, learned on other folds and applied held-out.

steps.title: Score all methods pooled
steps.detail: Report F1/QWK/MAE/acc/far-off/F1c2/F1c3 at pooled OOF n=1752 for every method vs the encoder baseline.

configs.methodology: Encoder = MentalBERT+CORN (soft probs). CoT = Qwen-7B greedy (Hybrid-W3) for routing; sc5 vote-fractions for prob-avg. Three combiners: (1) prob-avg 50/50 of encoder+sc5 soft probs; (2) severity-routed = CoT label if CoT>=2 else encoder; (3) nested-CV linear blend with leakage-free per-fold weight. Pooled OOF n=1752.

settings.value: use CoT label if CoT pred >=2 else encoder

results.note: recovers ~encoder MAE (0.684 vs enc 0.680) + highest acc 0.497, MAE-preserving alternative (CONFIRMED)
HEADLINE: beats both parents on macro-F1 and QWK; best severe F1 (c2 0.244, c3 0.295); worst MAE 0.759 (CONFIRMED)

configs.verdict: Severity-routing beats both parents simultaneously on macro-F1 (0.376 > CoT 0.373 > enc 0.348) AND QWK (0.367 > enc 0.354 > CoT 0.312) plus best severe-class F1, at the cost of worst MAE (0.759 — trusting CoT on severe calls inherits its far-off misses). prob-avg 50/50 is the MAE-preserving alternative (recovers ~encoder MAE + highest accuracy while still beating encoder macro-F1). CoT earns its place as an ENSEMBLE COMPONENT, not a standalone replacement. All six method rows + blend weights confirmed.

configs.full_name: STEP 4 — distillation to Qwen2.5-1.5B (teacher rationales -> LoRA student)
configs.summary: Distill the 7B CoT into a cheap 1.5B student via LoRA on label-conditioned teacher rationales — the student loses the severe-class recovery and is worse than the encoder, so the distillation win does not transfer.

steps.title: Generate teacher rationales
steps.detail: 7B teacher produces 1752 label-conditioned rationales (Hybrid-W3) -> outputs/cot/teacher_rationales_hybw3.jsonl, 0 parse fails.

steps.title: LoRA SFT the student
steps.detail: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, LoRA r16, 3 epochs, per-fold leakage-safe training via src/llm/distill_student.py + run_distill_*.sbatch.

steps.title: Generate distilled OOF
steps.detail: Run the per-fold student on held-out folds -> outputs/cot/folds_distill/.

steps.title: Compare to 7B and encoder
steps.detail: src/evaluation/distill_compare.py pools OOF n=1752 and reports F1/QWK/MAE/acc/F1c2/F1c3 vs 7B CoT and encoder.

steps.title: Route the student
steps.detail: Build severity-routed(enc, distilled) ensemble to check if a cheap student keeps the routing win.

configs.methodology: Teacher = Qwen2.5-7B (Hybrid-W3) label-conditioned rationales (n=1752). Student = Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, LoRA rank 16, 3 epochs, per-fold leakage-safe SFT. Greedy student decoding -> per-item PHQ-8 labels. Pooled OOF n=1752; compared to 7B CoT and encoder, plus severity-routed ensemble.

results.note: student lost the 7B's whole value-add; went backwards (CONFIRMED)
BELOW encoder on both, vs routed(enc,7B) 0.376/0.367 (CONFIRMED)

configs.verdict: A 1.5B student distilled from ~1400 label-conditioned rationales does NOT replace the 7B CoT: too little capacity / rare-class signal, and it loses the severe-class-3 recovery (0.295 -> 0.155) that was the 7B's whole value-add. Worse than the encoder on macro-F1; routing to its unreliable severe calls actively hurts. The 7B remains required for the ensemble win. Revisit options: bigger student (3B/7B), class-imbalance-aware SFT, more epochs/full-FT — or accept the 7B as a one-time offline component (~30 min/fold). All numbers confirmed from distill_compare_metrics.json.

configs.full_name: STEP 5 — better evidence (Hybrid-W5 + per-excerpt formatting), the standing-best ensemble
configs.summary: Widen retrieval to Hybrid-W5 and render evidence as numbered coherent excerpts instead of a shuffled keyword blob — standalone CoT macro-F1 dips, but the severity-routed ensemble reaches the best ordinal numbers (QWK 0.379) = standing best.

steps.title: Reformat evidence
steps.detail: cot_probe.format_evidence now renders retrieved_context_windows_hybrid_list JSON as numbered coherent excerpts instead of the shuffled _pack keyword blob.

steps.title: Widen to W5
steps.detail: Use Hybrid-W5 (5-window) retrieved evidence instead of W3; run greedy CoT 5-fold via run_cot_probe_w5.sbatch -> outputs/cot/folds_w5/.

steps.title: Score standalone CoT
steps.detail: Pool OOF n=1752 and compare W5 standalone CoT to W3 on macro-F1, accuracy, MAE, per-class F1.

steps.title: Rebuild ensembles
steps.detail: Recompute severity-routed(enc, W5-CoT), prob-avg, and nested-CV blend on the W5 evidence.

steps.title: Pick new best operating point
steps.detail: Confirm severity-routed(enc, W5-CoT) as the headline config and note the near-Pareto nested-CV blend over the encoder.

configs.methodology: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, no training, greedy. Evidence = Hybrid-W5 retrieved windows rendered as numbered per-excerpt text. Per-item independent scoring -> PHQ-8 0-3. Ensembles: severity-routed (CoT if >=2 else enc), prob-avg 50/50, nested-CV linear blend. Pooled OOF n=1752.

results.note: DOWN; class-2 F1 0.211->0.169 the main loss (CONFIRMED)
STANDING BEST; QWK 0.379 best ordinal of any CoT method (up from W3 0.367) (CONFIRMED)
W5 improves QWK + MAE, holds macro-F1 (CONFIRMED)
near-Pareto over encoder (MAE < enc 0.680, QWK ~= enc, F1 > enc) (CONFIRMED)

configs.verdict: Richer / de-fragmented evidence helps the COMBINATION's ordinal metrics (QWK/MAE), not CoT's standalone macro-F1 (which dips). New best config = severity-routed(encoder, W5-CoT): macro-F1 0.377, QWK 0.379, MAE 0.740 — the best ordinal agreement of any CoT method. Gains are small (~+0.012 QWK over W3), suggesting a data/label ceiling (top-2 acc 0.72 vs top-1 0.43). NOTE: prob-avg 50/50 with a hard one-hot CoT degenerates to the CoT prediction (verified: prob-avg row = CoT row 0.360/0.306); only meaningful with soft sc5 probs. All numbers confirmed.

configs.full_name: STEP 6 — far-off error analysis (W5 CoT) + learned stacking combiner
configs.summary: Read the far-off (>=2) CoT errors and test a learned LogReg stacker — errors are mostly a self-report/label ceiling and the stacker never dominates the hand severity-routing rule.

steps.title: Quantify far-off errors
steps.detail: 317/1752 (18%) far-off; 215 UNDER-predict (model 0/1, gold 2/3) vs 102 over; concentrated on Failure(65)/Appetite(54)/Concentrating(42)/Sleep(35) — somatic/internal items.

steps.title: Read ~24 cases
steps.detail: In both directions the CoT reasoning is largely FAITHFUL to the evidence, but the gold label diverges from what the interview content supports (self-report <-> interview-content gap).

steps.title: Classify error causes
steps.detail: Under-calls: symptom genuinely absent from interview. Over-calls: clear symptom language but low self-report. Small ~25% fixable slice = temporal reasoning (past/resolved symptoms counted as current) + frequency conservatism.

steps.title: Train learned stacker
steps.detail: src/evaluation/cot_stacker.py: nested-CV LogReg over encoder probs + CoT probs + item id, in balanced and unweighted variants.

steps.title: Compare stacker to routing
steps.detail: Check whether learned stacking beats the hand severity-routed(W5) rule on macro-F1/QWK/MAE.

configs.methodology: Qualitative read of 24 far-off cases on W5 CoT + learned stacking: nested-CV multinomial LogReg over [encoder CORN probs, CoT probs, item one-hot]; balanced (class-weighted) and unweighted variants. No GPU. Pooled OOF n=1752, compared to severity-routed(W5). NOTE: only the balanced stacker variant is in the saved cot_stacker_metrics.json; the unweighted variant numbers are memory-only.

settings.value: nested-CV LogReg over enc+CoT probs + item (class_weight='balanced' in saved script)

results.note: top-2 0.727 CONFIRMED from encoder probs; top-1 '0.43' is loose (encoder argmax-from-probs=0.457)
does not beat routing (CONFIRMED from cot_stacker_metrics.json)
MEMORY-ONLY; not in saved JSON (script only emits balanced); best MAE+acc but class-2 F1 collapses
none of the stacker operating points dominates it (CONFIRMED)

configs.verdict: The far-off errors are MOSTLY a real self-report <-> interview-content label ceiling (CoT reasoning is faithful; gold diverges), not a modeling gap — no prompt/evidence engineering on the transcript can close it. Only ~25% is fixable (temporal reasoning, frequency conservatism), and under/over-calls are opposite errors so net macro-F1 gain from nudging is limited. Learned stacking can sit anywhere on the F1<->MAE trade-off but never dominates the hand severity-routing rule. Verdict for the whole investigation: STOP tuning the CoT/evidence/combiner frontier; further gains need different LABELS (clinician ratings). Far-off counts/concentration and the balanced stacker confirmed; unweighted stacker numbers are memory-only.

configs.full_name: STEP 7 — item-aware BM25 retrieval (symptom-vocabulary query expansion)
configs.summary: Expand each item's BM25 query with symptom vocabulary; downstream-validated +0.034 macro-F1 over matched BM25-base, but both BM25 conditions stay below the production hybrid retriever.

steps.title: Per-item retrieval diagnostic
steps.detail: src/evaluation/retrieval_window_analysis.py: keyword-hit rate of hybrid retrieval varies wildly (Sleep 0.90 vs Moving 0.35, Appetite ~0.54); kw-hit<->far-off corr only r=-0.13 (memory-only; confounded by label skew, e.g. Moving 77% y=0).

steps.title: Build item-aware query
steps.detail: src/retrieval/item_aware_retrieval.py prototype expands each item's BM25 query with symptom vocabulary; offline kw-hit +0.17 vs bare-BM25 (circular caveat).

steps.title: Downstream CoT test
steps.detail: run_cot_itemaware.sbatch: non-circular test holding bank/k fixed, only query differs; CoT 5-fold pooled n=1752 vs matched bm25-base control.

steps.title: Per-item attribution
steps.detail: Check where gains land (Sleep, Failure, Appetite, Depressed) and where regressions occur (NoInterest, Tired, Concentrating).

configs.methodology: BM25 retrieval with symptom-vocabulary query expansion per item vs matched bare-BM25 control (same bank/k, only query differs). Evidence fed to greedy Qwen-7B CoT, per-item scoring. Pooled OOF n=1752. Diagnostic via retrieval_window_analysis.py (keyword-hit rate).

results.value: both BM25 < hybrid-W5 CoT (0.360/0.306) and encoder (0.348)
results.note: closes most of bm25->hybrid gap, doesn't beat hybrid (CONFIRMED)

configs.verdict: The item-aware lever is REAL and downstream-validated (non-circular): symptom-vocabulary query expansion adds +0.034 macro-F1 / +0.060 QWK over matched BM25, with gains landing exactly where retrieval improved (Sleep/Failure/Appetite/Depressed). BUT both BM25 conditions remain below the production hybrid-W5 CoT and the encoder. To beat the pipeline, apply expansion to the HYBRID retriever (STEP 8). Failure/Moving stayed low even with expansion -> those symptoms aren't verbalized (ceiling confirmed from the retrieval side). Downstream metrics + offline kw-hit confirmed; the r=-0.13 correlation is memory-only.

configs.full_name: STEP 8 — item-aware HYBRID retrieval (MiniLM semantic + BM25, item-aware query expansion)
configs.summary: Reimplement a MiniLM+BM25 hybrid retriever and add item-aware query expansion — semantic retrieval already captures topical relevance, so item-awareness adds zero macro-F1 and the whole reimpl trails production.

steps.title: Reimplement hybrid retriever
steps.detail: src/retrieval/hybrid_retrieval.py: MiniLM mean-pooled embeddings via transformers, min-max-norm 0.5*sem + 0.5*BM25, k=5, W5 bank context_window_bank.json.

steps.title: Build item-aware hybrid dataset
steps.detail: Apply symptom-vocabulary query expansion to the hybrid retriever -> phq8_item_dataset_hybrid_itemaware_w5.csv.

steps.title: Run CoT on both conditions
steps.detail: run_cot_hybrid_itemaware.sbatch: hybrid-bare vs item-aware-hybrid, greedy CoT 5-fold pooled n=1752.

steps.title: Compare within-hybrid and vs production
steps.detail: Measure item-aware delta within the reimpl hybrid and benchmark both against production W5-hybrid CoT + the standing-best ensemble.

configs.methodology: Reimplemented hybrid retriever: MiniLM mean-pooled embeddings, min-max normalized score = 0.5*semantic + 0.5*BM25, k=5, W5 bank. Item-aware = same retriever with symptom-vocabulary query expansion. Greedy Qwen-7B CoT. Pooled OOF n=1752. Ensembles: severity-routed(enc, item-aware-hybrid), nested-CV blend.

settings.value: MiniLM mean-pooled + BM25, 0.5/0.5 min-max-norm, k=5, W5 bank

results.note: item-aware macro-F1 gain = ZERO (0.326->0.325), unlike BM25 (+0.034) (CONFIRMED)
MiniLM/alpha=0.5 reimpl weaker than off-branch hybrid (CONFIRMED)
BELOW standing best 0.377/0.379; nested-CV blend down-weighted weak CoT to w~=0.1 (CONFIRMED)

configs.verdict: Item-aware query expansion's value is real for WEAK retrieval (BM25) but SUBSUMED by good semantic retrieval: within the hybrid reimpl it adds ZERO macro-F1 (0.326->0.325), because semantic retrieval already captures topical relevance (it does lift QWK +0.055 / c3 +0.051 but worsens MAE). Both reimpl conditions trail production W5-hybrid CoT and the ensemble does not beat standing best. Caveat: the reimpl hybrid != production hybrid, so this tests 'cheap item-aware hybrid', not item-awareness on the real production retriever. Standing best unchanged. All numbers confirmed.

configs.full_name: STEP 9 — MentaLLaMA domain LLM as the CoT backbone (13B-4bit and 7B-bf16)

Compared to Qwen-7B CoT. Only fold-1-style runs exist (single fold-1 CSV per variant); exact pooled metrics + parse-fail rates are memory-only — findings are qualitative.

Three backbones tested (MentaLLaMA 13B-4bit & 7B-bf16, LLaMA-2 base); all over-predicted with high parse-fail and lost to Qwen-7B, which remains the CoT model.

steps.detail: Realize full DAIC transcripts are median ~1.3k tokens (max 4.5k) but CoT had been fed only ~350 tokens of retrieved windows — retrieval was an artifact of the encoder's 512 limit, not needed for the 32k-context LLM.

steps.title: Feed whole transcript

steps.title: Measure severe recovery

steps.title: Per-item attribution
steps.detail: Decompose gains/losses by item to find which symptoms benefit from full context vs focused retrieval.

steps.title: Re-run ensembles
steps.detail: Build severity-routed and nested-CV blend on full-transcript CoT and compare to standing best.

configs.methodology: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (32k ctx), no training, greedy. Evidence = full DAIC transcript per item (no retrieval). Per-item scoring -> PHQ-8 0-3. Pooled OOF n=1752. Compared to retrieved-W5 CoT and standing-best ensemble; severity-routed + nested-CV blend recomputed.

settings.value: full transcript (median ~1.3k tok, max 4.5k); no retrieval

results.note: DECISIVE: severe misses were ~half a retrieval miss, not pure label ceiling (CONFIRMED: W5 under-far-off=215, full=105)

configs.verdict: Partly OVERTURNS the label-ceiling claim: full context HALVES under-called-severe misses (215->105), proving the severe misses were ~half a RETRIEVAL miss, not pure label ceiling — full context recovers symptoms retrieval hid. BUT it causes OVER-attribution (far-off 317->451, MAE worse), so net macro-F1 drops; gains land on evidence-starved items (Appetite/NoInterest), losses on well-retrieved ones (Depressed/Sleep/Moving). INVESTIGATION CONCLUDED: every scaling/distillation/model/retrieval/evidence lever tested and bounded; residual ceiling is part-retrieval (fixable, item-dependent) part-label (needs clinician ratings). All numbers recomputed and confirmed.

configs.full_name: Joint single-shot whole-picture CoT (overall impression then 8 scores)
configs.summary: One LLM call scores all 8 PHQ-8 items at once: form a one-sentence overall impression, then emit 8 scores; baseline whole-picture variant.

steps.title: Assemble per-item evidence
steps.detail: For each participant, build one user block with Hybrid-W3 retrieved keyword-like snippets for all 8 PHQ-8 items (ITEM 1..8 with the question text and snippets, or '(no snippets retrieved)').

steps.title: Compute per-item confidence

steps.title: Apply vote gate

steps.title: Sweep tau
steps.detail: With --sweep the code reports vote<0.6, vote<0.8, vote<1.0 (tau=1.0 routes effectively all items where the LLM isn't unanimous).

configs.methodology: Cascade combiner. Backbone: pooled 10-chain CoT LLM (primary) + MentalBERT-CORN-W3 encoder (tiebreaker). No loss (inference fusion). Evidence: LLM vote fractions (gate) + LLM top-2 candidates and encoder prob_0..3 (tiebreak). Gate: stat = maxp < tau, tau in {0.6, 0.8, 1.0}. Decoding: LLM argmax kept; on gated items pred = top2[argmax(encP[top2])]. The vote gate is the statistical leg of the merged gate. Verified present in gate_mask; standalone numbers not persisted to JSON.

steps.title: Sweep threshold
